SECTION I Informational Matters COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: MTH 103, Applied Precalculus Add online section Linear, quadratic, power, exponential, logarithmic and periodic functions - their graphs and properties.
Emphasis on interpretation and real-life applications, examples and modeling.
Not for major credit in mathematics.
Not intended for students planning to take MTH 111 or MTH 141. (Lec. 3) MTH 244, Differential Equations Add online section (3 crs.) Classification and solution of differential equations involving one independent variable.
Applications to the physical sciences.
Basics for further study in applied mathematics and for advanced work in physics and engineering. (Lec. 3) Pre: MTH 142.

MUS 280, Mid-program Portfolio in Music Delete course (0 crs.) Individual accomplishment of activities and experiences, demonstrating interest and competency in music at the midpoint in the student's program of studies as a music major. (Portfolio) Pre: sophomore standing in music.
MUS 480, Graduation Portfolio Delete course (0-2 crs.) Seminar covering topics and the development of a graduation portfolio appropriate to the student's degree program.
The portfolio shows accomplishments from throughout the degree program and achievement of competencies indicating potential success as a graduate. (Portfolio) Pre: MUS 280 or permission of chairperson and senior standing in music.
For music education majors, concurrent enrollment in EDC 484 required.
To be taken during the last semester of coursework in the major.
May be repeated.
Not for graduate credit. 1

COLLEGE OF PHARMACY: BPS 334, Pharmacology and Medicinal Chemistry of Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Delete course (2 crs.) Mechanism of action, adverse effects, and therapeutic applications of drugs affecting cardiovascular and renal function. (Lec. 2) Pre: Doctor of Pharmacy professional student in good standing; or permission of instructor.
SECTION II Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation by the Faculty Senate COURSES CHANGES: COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: PRS/JOR 340, Public Relations Strategies Change title, prerequisite (3 crs.) Cross-listed as (PRS), JOR 340.
Principles and procedures in public relations: emphasis on role of the public relations practitioner as a specialist in communication; analysis of publications produced as a part of public relations. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: Declared PR majors or PR minors, PRS100.
COLLEGE OF PHARMACY: BPS 301, Pharmaceutics I: Biopharmaceutics Change title, description, prerequisites (2 crs.) Application of kinetics to stability, dissolution, absorption, and other biopharmaceutical processes.
Bioavailability and generic equivalence. (Lec. 2) BSPS majors with junior standing and above.
CHE students by permission number only.

BPS 313, Principles of Medicinal Chemistry Change prerequisites (2 crs.) Physico-chemical properties of drug molecules; and principles needed to understand chemical basis of pharmacology and therapeutics, pharmacophores for drugs used to treat disease, and structure-activity relationships of drug-target interactions. (Lec. 2) Pre: BSPS majors with junior standing and above and CHM 228.
BPS 325, Human Drug Metabolism Change title, description, prerequisites (2 crs.) Chemical, biochemical, genetic, clinical and pre-clinical aspects of drug metabolism. (Lec. 2) Pre: BSPS majors with junior standing and above and BPS301.
BPS 401, Pharmaceutical Pharmacology I Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Mechanisms underlying both the therapeutic and toxic actions of currently available drugs including Autonomic and Central Nervous system agents and Cardiovascular system agents.
First of 2-semester sequence. (Lec. 3) Pre: BSPS majors with junior standing or above, BIO222, and CMB311.
Not for graduate credit. 2

BPS 425, GMPs in the Manufacture of Pharmaceutical Products Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Application of current Good Manufacturing Practices to the manufacture and quality control of various pharmaceutical products. (Lec. 3) Pre: BSPS majors with junior standing or above and BPS315.
CHE majors with permission number.
BPS 443, Formulation and Manufacturing Laboratory Change prerequisites (2 crs.) Provides general principles and hands-on experience in the preformulation, formulation, manufacturing, and quality control fields that are necessary in design, formulation, compounding and manufacturing of drug dosage forms. (Lab. 4) Pre: BSPS majors with junior standing or above and BPS 315.
BPS 451, Techniques in Medicinal Chemistry and Molecular Biology Change prerequisites (4 crs.) Provides students with an understanding of medicinal chemistry, molecular biology, and drug analysis techniques commonly used in pharmaceutical industry.
The course combines laboratory exercises with easy-to-understand lectures. (Lec. 3, Lab. 4) Pre: BSPS majors with senior standing.

BPS 460, Pharmaceutical Science Internship/Field Experience Changes credits, allow to be repeated (0, 3 ,6, 9, or 12 crs.) Undergraduate BS Pharmaceutical Science majors completing approved Off Campus Experience.
Fall, Spring, or Summer Semester.
Registration is by permission number only. (Practicum) Pre: Permission number required.
May be repeated for a maximum of 12 credits.
Not for graduate credit.
COLLEGE OF EDUCATION AND PROFESSIONAL STUDIES: EDC 484, Practical Teaching Residency II Change title, description, prerequisites (6-12 crs.) Engage in an intensive, full teaching load that provides deep instructional practice and experiences related to school-based professional requirements. (Pract.) Pre: methods course(s) of secondary, middle level, elementary, early childhood, music, and world languages education.
Not for graduate credit.
